text:
nina: quick check — prepping rollout for the prefix-cache header change, want to lock semantics before the canary. proposal: single response header `X-RW-Cache` with values `hit|partial|miss` and an optional `prefix=<sha256>` param. thoughts?
sam: ok on single header, but streaming clients currently parse headers only at the start of the stream. we need to ensure header is emitted before first chunk or clients will miss the flag.
alex: +1 on single header. example format I like: `X-RW-Cache: hit; prefix=5f2a...; scope=org/123` — keeps parsing trivial.
maria: prefer keep name short. maybe `X-RW-Cache: hit;prefix=SHA256(...)`. also we should avoid leaking full keys — prefix hash only.
nina: agreed on hashing. also need to decide Cache-Control semantics: should prefix-cached responses include `Cache-Control`? current thought: always include `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60` for short TTL, unless request has `sensitive=true` then `no-store`.
sam: TTL derivation needs to be deterministic. suggest server uses model-config TTL + request-level `max_prefix_ttl` override. note: for prefix responses we must surface a new header `X-RW-Cache-TTL` (seconds) so clients can make local decisions.
ops-bot: FYI: invalidation webhook endpoint `/internal/cache/invalidate` exists for Dedicated; public API planned.
alex: on invalidation API — we should accept either `key=` (full) or `prefix=` (hash) and return `202` + list of shards touched. example POST body:```json
{
  "prefix": "5f2a...",
  "scope": "org/123"
}
```
maria: question: backward compatibility. older SDKs expect `X-RW-Cache-Hit: true` boolean. plan: emit both `X-RW-Cache` and `X-RW-Cache-Hit` during rollout for 2 weeks, with `X-RW-Cache-Hit` mapping `hit->true, miss->false`. add `X-RW-Cache-V: 2` to indicate new schema.
nina: good call. I'll add compatibility header. also need to confirm streaming library will not duplicate header per chunk; Sam, can you check the runtime patch? @sam
sam: looking — runtime currently attaches headers at response start; streaming shim re-sends status but not new headers. I left a small change in PR #456 to emit headers in the initial metadata frame. pinged @alex for review.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled for wednesday 10:00 PST -> eng-platform/canary (4 nodes) :rocket:
nina: small ops question: if we invalidate a prefix while inflight requests are using cached KV, do we block or let them finish? my preference: let in-flight finish, mark cache entry stale and evict after. Thoughts?
alex: let them finish. evict asynchronously. critical to avoid tail latency spikes from synchronous invalidation.
maria: agree — add a `stale=true` marker header on responses served while eviction in progress so observability can track. e.g., `X-RW-Cache-Stale: 1`.
sam: PR note: streaming clients need header emitted before chunk; I left a test case in `runtime/streaming/test_headers.py`. coverage added.
nina: thanks. i'll update the spec doc and add a short migration checklist (emit both headers, add `X-RW-Cache-V`, ensure header on initial stream frame, wire invalidation API). will ping infra and devex. PR #456 is primary. @sam please review today if possible.
ops-bot: reminder: feature flags `prefix_cache_v2` will gate rollout in prod.
maria: added a comment about not exposing raw prefix in logs — redact hashing in traces.
alex: noted — telemetry will only log `prefix_hash` and `scope`.
sam: reviewing now, small nit about header parsing util. will push patch soon.
nina: perfect, thanks all :thumbsup:
